chunks: (3) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated: Ali ibn Ibraheem ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus and Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say:
The earth does not remain empty of a scholar (Imam), so that if the believers add something (to the religion), he corrects them, and if they omit something, he completes it for them.

key_terms.عَالِمٌ: Scholar/Imam (specifically the divinely appointed guide in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the role of the Imam or Scholar in preserving the religion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the necessity of the *Hujjah* (Proof of God) to maintain religious continuity between prophethood and the final resurrection. It highlights the Imam’s dual role as a preserver of orthodoxy against innovation (*ziyadah*) and a restorer of neglected practices (*nuqsan*), ensuring the community remains on the straight path. This concept is foundational to the Shia belief in the infallible guidance provided by the Ahl al-Bayt.
